sources.entry: Exim - Message transfer agent (MTA) developed at the University of Cambridge. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C/deb

summary.name: Exim
summary.one_liner: Exim is a message transfer agent (MTA) for Unix systems connected to the Internet, originally developed at the University of Cambridge and released under the GNU GPL.
use_cases: Routing email between mail servers on a Unix system
Replacing Sendmail with a different MTA
Running an SMTP mail server on Linux or Unix
summary.what_it_does: Exim is a message transfer agent that moves and routes email on Unix systems connected to the Internet. The page says it offers a great deal of flexibility in how mail is routed. It includes extensive facilities for checking incoming mail. It can be installed in place of Sendmail, though its configuration differs. The page describes its style as similar to Smail 3 but with more general facilities. The current version listed is 4.100.1, which is a security release.
notable: Can be installed as a drop-in replacement for Sendmail
Free under the GNU General Public Licence (GPL-3.0 per awesome-selfhosted listing)
caveats: Configuration is quite different from Sendmail
Versions before 4.100.1 are obsolete, and the 3.x line should not be used
Beta versions are available but not recommended unless you are willing to work with beta software
